Pathankot through Ruchi Mehta & Ajay Mehta, with the allegations of cheating,
fraud, misrepresentation, misappropriation & money laundering.
After detailed enquiry an FIR No. 126 dated 01.11.2024, under section 420 of IPC registered at Police Station Sujanpur, District Pathankot against the petitioner Ruchi Mehta."

4. The petitioner's counsel prays for bail by imposing any stringent conditions and contends that further pre-trial incarceration would cause an irreversible injustice to the petitioner and their family.

5. Counsel for the petitioner argued as follows:-
"2. That for the proper adjudication of the matter in hand, the account statement of the petitioner is required to be placed on record reflecting the amount transferred by the petitioner in the account of the complainant amounting to 1.63 lakhs and on demanding the same but the petitioner from the complainant, the complainant had been threatening and abusing the petitioner regarding which various complaints have been filed and even even protection petition has been filed before this Hon'ble court bearing CRWP No 2354 of 2024 and out of all this false FIR has been got registered by the complainant.
Photocopy of the account statement of the petitioner is hereby attached as Annexure P- 11.
That not even a single penny has been transferred by the complainant in the account of the petitioner and three different FIR against the complainant.

That the whole dispute is regarding demanding money by the petitioner/applicant from the complainant and in order to escape her liability the complainant has been adopting illegal methods such as threatening, abusing,
blackmailing and even man handling in the police station and now a false FIR has been got registered by stating that the complainant who is facing criminal prosecution of Excise Act and is in the business of selling illicit liquor has been cheated on the protest of huge returns and gave 32 lakhs in cash."
6. The State's counsel opposes bail and refers to the reply.

One day the petitioner told Vinayka (niece of complainant) that she is running "Rajput Finance Company" and "Ujwal Bharat Sanstha" company situated at Gandhi Chowk Pathankot.
These are finance companies and these companies are running on very high scale and further told her that any person who invest in her company then they used to give them huge profit.

On this Vinayka (niece of the complainant) talked with the complainant about investing money in the Ruchi Mehta's Company.
The complainant along with Vinayka went to the office of the Ruchi Mehta at Gandhi Chowk Pathankot for Nofurther information.
The said Ruchi Mehta had installed hording of her company outside her office.
In the office of Ruchi Mehta, Ruchi Mehta and her mother Nirmala Devi were present.

That Ruchi Mehta went to the house of the complainant and convinced her that if she invested rupees 5 Lakhs in her company then she will return 6 Lakhs in two months to the complainant.
The complainant fell in rosy words of the petitioner and in the month of May 2023 gave an amount of Rs. 5 Lakhs to Ruchi Mehta for investing in her "Rajput Finance company".
The petitioner paid three installments of Rs. 10,000/- each to the complainant in small span of time.
On dated 30.06.2023, the petitioner again demanded Rs.4,50,000/- from the complainant and told her that she will return an amount of Rs. 11 Lakhs to the complainant within 2 months.

The complainant again fell into the rosy words of the petitioner and paid an amount of Rs.
4,50,000/- in cash.
After the period of 2 months i.e. in the month of September 2023, the complainant demanded her money back from the petitioner but.
the petitioner told the complainant to wait for one month and she will pay an amount of Rs. 12,00,000/- in the month of October 2023.

The complainant trusted the petitioner and thereafter in the month of December 2023, the complainant again demanded her money but the petitioner told her that her company business is decreased and requested her to wait for some more time.

On this the complainant told the petitioner that her son is getting marry on 06.02.2024 and requested her to return the amount before his marriage and the petitioner convinced the complainant that she will return the said amount before the marriage of complainant's son.

On 13.01.2024 the petitioner came to the house of the complainant and took away Gold Articles to the tune of Rs. 4,21,000/- on the pretext that she will return all the Gold Article along with interest at the time of marriage of her son.

After some days Ruchi Mehta came to the house of complainant and started saying that she is in need of Rs.
4,00,000/- and requested the complainant to give her Rs. 4,00,000/- and promised her that she will return all the amounts before the marriage of complainant's son.
The complainant fell into the words of the petitioner and give her an amount of Rs. 4,00,000/- in cash.
But the petitioner did not return the money as promised by her.

Moreover, the petitioner had also mortgage the Gold Articles of the complainant for an amount of Rs. 5,00,000/- to "Vikas Jewellers" and further received an additional amountof Rs. 2,00,000/- as loan.
The complainant had also given an amount of Rs. 2,00,000/- after taking loan from "Saini Property Dealers".

The petitioner had committed cheating with the complainant after taking undue advantage of her trust and commit cheating to the tune of Rs.

5C. Documentary Proof & Evidence Against the petitioner:-
That the complainant during enquiry had provided with the such as Screen Shots of the payments made to the petitioner through mobile transactions, the hand written receipts of the documents i.e. the receipts issued by the petitioner/accused "Vikas Jeweller"
from which she had raised the money after mortgaging the Gold Articles of complainant, were handed over by the complainant to the police during the enquiry conducted by DSP Pathankot to prove the fact that she had given money on the demand of petitioner/accused.
It is further detailed by the complainant in her statement the most part of the amount was given in cash to the complainant.
During the course of Enquiry, the statements of witnesses were also recorded qua the factum that the complainant had given the money to the petitioner."

8. The submissions made by the petitioner prima facie appear to be somewhat probable, however these observations are made only for the purpose of considering bail and shall have no bearing on investigation or trial which should be done independently.
It is neither a case of custodial interrogation nor pre-trial incarceration.
9. Pre-trial incarceration should not be a replica of post-conviction sentencing.

The evidence might be prima facie sufficient to launch prosecution or to frame charges, but this Court is not considering the evidence at that stage but is analyzing it for the stage of anticipatory bail.
An analysis of the above does not justify custodial interrogation or pre- trial incarceration.

10. Given the above, the penal provisions invoked coupled with the primafacie analysis of the nature of allegations and the other factors peculiar to this case, there would be no justifiability for custodial interrogation or the pre-trial incarceration at this stage.

Without commenting on the case's merits,
in the facts and circumstances peculiar to this case, and for the reasons mentioned above, the petitioner makes a case for bail.
